newsitem.title: CHINA: China says Iraq 'prisoner' to no-fly zones.
newsitem.headline: China says Iraq 'prisoner' to no-fly zones.

text.p: China on Tuesday slammed the no-fly zones imposed over Iraq, saying the zones had made Baghdad a virtual prisoner and violated its sovereignty.

"Many of the world's nations hold that the no-fly zones were established by some Western countries on their own accord...and that they were not directly empowered by the U.N.," said the Liberation Army Daily, the official mouthpiece for China's armed forces.
The newspaper said the no-fly zones imposed by Western allies after the 1991 Gulf War and extended by Washington after its recent missle attacks against Iraqi targets were an act of aggression.
Extension of the zones would give Washington a pretext to launch further strikes on Iraq by restricting where Baghdad could send its armies, the newspaper said.
"Any military action taken can be seen as a 'violation' and air strikes carried out," it said. "The restricted country becomes a prisoner that has been placed under house arrest."
The newspaper said the presence of U.S. forces in the Persian Gulf undermined regional security.
"America's so-called 'Operation Desert Strike' was entirely a hegemonic act of aggression against a sovereign state," it said in a reference to the missile attacks.

China has voiced strong displeasure over U.S. cruise missile attacks against Iraq earlier this month, accusing U.S. President Bill Clinton of using the strikes to boost his popularity in an election year.
The strikes were in retaliation for intervention by Iraqi forces in Kurdish factional fighting in northern Iraq.
